authority_basis.summary: Pursue canonical prime-power and Frobenius operations after auditing whether primes are inherited.

operations.title: Canonical primary operations exist but do not yield Frobenius
operations.statement: For H_d=(Z/d)^(d-2), canonical p-primary subgroups and scalar operators P_p=p exist with P_p^r=P_(p^r), and their kernel filtration recovers v_p(d). But P_p is nilpotent, zero modulo p, and contains no information beyond d. Existing Adams operations commute across a kernel only for indices coprime to its exponent, so psi^p fails on nontrivial p-primary kernels; tested absolute Frobenius collapses the bad fiber. No nontrivial arithmetic Frobenius is thereby derived.
operations.scope: Algebraic norm module and established Adams-Mackey gates; no geometric or physical Frobenius.

operations.title: Prime-primary Frobenius hostile test
operations.procedure: On H_(p)=(Z/p^a)^(d-2), iterate P_p=p. Verify P_p^a=0 and its reduction on H_(p)/pH_(p) is zero. Compare the Adams-Mackey criterion gcd(p,exp K)=1 for a nontrivial p-primary kernel.
operations.expected_result: Strict scalar prime-power composition holds, but the operator is nilpotent and psi^p fails Mackey compatibility. A nontrivial unit-eigenvalue or compatible Frobenius spectrum would falsify the negative verdict.
